title: A more polished home for dea

changes.text: An interactive voice channel preview shows how dea helps keep a round in sync.
A fresh bat icon gives dea a new look across the site.
The changelog and command pages are easier to browse, with clearer controls and more room to read.
The home page now shows the live command count, with clearer status details and a more comfortable light theme.
A new home page introduces dea's voice-round tools, commands and live service status.
The commands and changelog pages make it easier to explore what dea can do and what's new.
Light and dark themes and a responsive layout make the site comfortable on phones and desktops.
Voice logs now describe joins, leaves, moves and mute changes in plain language.
Quick voice changes are grouped together, so busy rounds create fewer log messages.
Deleted-message logs explain when Discord does not identify who removed a message.
Moderator actions are easier to identify in deletion and audit logs.
Deleted-message entries now attribute actions more reliably.

title: Guild data stays with the bot

changes.text: Server settings and saved round details now persist in hosted PostgreSQL storage.
The deployment no longer depends on a local persistent disk.
Saved lobby codes and the dead-player list are restored when dea comes back online.
The bot presence now shows its current uptime.
A public status dashboard shows the bot connection, server count, gateway ping and process uptime.
The health page refreshes automatically while it is open.
Server logs include clearer event details and command activity.
Deleted-message logs can show image attachments directly in the entry.
Actor attribution is more reliable for Discord audit events.
